one_line_description.value: Ramp is a spend-management and finance automation platform covering bill pay, corporate cards, reimbursements, procurement and spend controls, with a public developer API.
one_line_description.quote: Bill Pay Bills, draft bills, payments, vendors, 3-way match.

has_public_api.quote: Canonical OpenAPI schema for the Developer API: /openapi/developer-api.json.

api_breadth.value: REST, read-write across ~30 scoped resource areas (cards, bills, payments, users, accounting, procurement, reimbursements)
api_breadth.quote: | `cards:write` | Cards | Create, update, and manage cards |

auth_methods.quote: Your app gets an access token from `/developer/v1/token`, authenticating with its client ID and secret (typically HTTP Basic Auth), and scopes control what the token can access.

oauth_scopes_documented.quote: | `accounting:read` | Accounting data | Access accounting sync status and metadata |

access_model.quote: Don't have a Ramp account? Request a sandbox to start building right away.

access_notes.value: Existing Ramp customers self-serve credentials in-product (Company → Developer) and then make API calls; developers without a Ramp account must request sandbox access (demo.ramp.com / demo-api.ramp.com); building an integration for other businesses routes through Ramp's partner program.
access_notes.quote: Building an integration for other businesses? Start with the partner program.

official_mcp_server.quote: claude mcp add --transport http ramp https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp

webhooks.quote: Ramp delivers `*.created`, `*.updated`, `*.ready_to_sync`, and other event types over HTTPS to your registered URL.

sandbox_or_test_env.quote: The Ramp sandbox is a testing environment where developers and partners can safely build, test, and experiment with Ramp's API without affecting live production data.

verdict_reason: Ramp documents a public REST Developer API with OAuth 2.0 (client credentials, authorization code, refresh, JWT bearer grants), a large read-write scope catalog, webhooks, a canonical OpenAPI schema, and a sandbox. However, credentials require either an existing Ramp business account or a requested sandbox, and integrations for other businesses go through the partner program. That gating keeps it out of the easy tier despite strong API breadth.
main_blocker: Credentials require an existing Ramp account or an approved sandbox request
outreach_reason: Developers without a Ramp account must request sandbox access from Ramp, and building on behalf of other businesses requires joining the Ramp partner program.
open_questions: Numeric rate limits were not captured: the limits page (docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/api/limits) returned a JavaScript shell in the evidence; only a general 'Rate limits and timeouts' convention link was visible.
No official vendor-maintained SDK/client library was found in the captured pages; the only dev tooling mentioned is the Ramp CLI and the OpenAPI schema.
API versioning/deprecation policy was not readable; the developer terms page (ramp.com/legal/developer-terms/...) was surfaced in search but not included in the evidence bundle.

Whether a free self-serve Ramp signup grants API credential creation, and whether sandbox requests are auto-approved, could not be verified because the pricing page text was only a search snippet, not a citable source.
The scope table in the authorization page was truncated after 'receipt_integrations', so the full scope catalog is not captured.

extra_evidence.quote: Have a Ramp account? Create credentials and make your first API call.
Ramp runs two MCP servers, one for your Ramp account and one for Ramp Data benchmarks.

audit.notes: Pricing and developer-tools pages appeared only in search snippets and were excluded as non-citable; access_model classified as admin_approval because sandbox access is requested and partner builds require the partner program.
